title: Retirement-owned person debt, and RoutedRecord's actor domain
founderRuling: Do not invest reconstruction effort in canonicalizing person identity inside code already governed for removal. Those sites become RETIREMENT_OWNED STRUCTURAL DEBT: still real debt, still visible, discharged only by physical deletion — not by bookkeeping, not by detector exclusion.

routedRecord.exactAmbiguityBefore: `authorHandle: _opt(authorRaw, ['handle', 'handleOrSlug'])`. Because `handleOrSlug` is the normalised field a PERSON's handle and an INSTITUTION's slug share, a consumer holding this value could not know which authority owned it — and the model carried no actorType to say.

resolution.finding: The union did not exist. The producer has one branch, and it is a person selected with the canonical person projection. `handleOrSlug` is never sent on this contract. The client had invented an ambiguity the server never had.
resolution.action: The author is now `AuraPersonIdentity`, read by the canonical reader. `authorName` and `authorHandle` remain as accessors, so no consumer changed.
resolution.authorityReused: AuraPersonIdentity — preferred order option 1/3: consume the existing canonical authority, and preserve the producer's single person branch rather than flattening it into an ambiguous value.
resolution.whatWasNotDone: No universal Actor model was invented. No actorType was added to discriminate a union of one. PERSON and INSTITUTION identity authorities were not merged. No new representation was introduced.
resolution.semanticPropertyMet: A consumer now determines the identity domain from the TYPE — `RoutedRecord.author` is an `AuraPersonIdentity`. Nothing is inferred from string shape, route prefix, avatar presence, fallback values or UI context.
resolution.governedNonPromotion: `authorName` returns null when the producer named nobody, because both screens hide the byline row when it is empty and the shared neutral word would print 'Someone' under a post. The ORDER is canonical; only the nullability is the surface's.

nonIdentityDefectObserved.observation: The producer emits the post text as `text`, not `body`, and no `postBody` key exists on the DTO. On the real contract `record.postBody` therefore resolves to null and both engagement screens omit the post body entirely.
nonIdentityDefectObserved.action: NOT FIXED. It is not identity, and this task authorizes an identity correction. Reported so it is not lost.

f053.structuralTest: Can one Aura person acquire different identity semantics across surfaces? In the surviving product, NO. In the legacy correspondence and messages surfaces, YES — CorrespondenceIdentity names an unresolved person 'Member' and 'Member {id}' where the canonical reader says 'Someone', and it accepts alias orders the canonical reader does not.
f053.dimensionalReport: SURVIVING-PRODUCT PERSON IDENTITY: canonical. LEGACY-RETIREMENT DEBT: 15 sites, blocking finding-level completion. Both dimensions are reported here without inventing a new finding state; the finding itself stays PARTIALLY_VALIDATED.
f053.notInvisible: The legacy semantics are not treated as absent merely because product direction says the surfaces will retire. They can execute today.
